newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse continues its bull-run.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse continues its bull-run.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange shrugged off anxiety on European markets on Tuesday ahead of a speech by U.S. Fed chairman Alan Greenspan and continued its rally to a second successive record level on Tuesday.
The BUX index finished at 5,276.51 points, up 141.20.

"The market's basic pattern has been the same," said Istvan Simon of Concorde Securities. "American funds have a lot of money to spend, the country's assessment is good and the number of Hungarian companies (in which they can invest) is limited."
However, Simon noted that many foreign investors have already become more cautious with their purchases on the Budapest bourse, which has risen more than 25 percent since the beginning of the year.
But domestic investors have remained active on the market, traders said.
Chemicals issue Borsodchem remained in the forefront and continued to benefit from a "buy" recommendation by ING Barings on the issue yesterday.

The stock, which began its rally on the back of news that Borsodchem expected to receive up to 100 percent tax relief for 1997 stemming from the country's tax regulations, surged another nine percent today to end at 6,375 forints, up 525, but below the day's peak of 6,500.
"Although it is far from certain, the market already takes it for granted that Borsodchem will receive the tax relief," Simon said. "So, Borsodchem is lifting off and dragging others with it".
